# PR 2 — Register declared secrets at the run boundary; redact them from events and errors

**Self-contained implementation plan.** Everything needed to implement this is
in this file plus the repository. It is the spine of a series of secrets/
redaction PRs; it has **no prerequisites** beyond what is already merged on
main. (Two merged foundations it builds on: `fabro_redact::SecretRedactor`
exists, and `secrets.NAME` tokens already resolve from the vault at the run
boundary.)

> **Token notation.** Interpolation tokens are written in this file without
> their enclosing double curly braces, so the file is safe to pass directly as
> a workflow goal (the goal templater would otherwise try to expand them).
> Read `secrets.NAME`, `env.NAME` as the double-curly-brace token form used in
> the codebase, and write the real double-brace syntax in the code, tests, and
> docs you produce.

## Context and goal

Fabro workflows can declare vault secrets in run config via `secrets.NAME`
tokens (MCP transport env, run-environment env, prepare-step commands/env,
docker config). Those tokens resolve server-side at the run boundary in
`RunSession::new`. Redaction of run output (events, `progress.jsonl`, error
text) is currently **content-based only**: pattern + entropy matching in
`fabro-redact`. Content-based matching is structurally blind to a *declared*
secret whose value looks ordinary — e.g. a secret whose value is `staging`,
`db-prod-3`, or `hunter2` trips neither entropy nor any pattern rule, and
today leaks **verbatim** into emitted events and error messages. That is a
live gap: the user explicitly declared the value secret, and the system does
not honor it.

**Goal:** register every resolved declared-secret value into a per-run
exact-match registry at the single place secrets resolve, and apply that
registry (composed after the content-based pass) to the run's structured
output surfaces: emitted events and setup-failure error text.

Design rules (fixed — the "why" for each is inline):

1. **One registration point.** Every secret value flows through the one
   boundary lookup closure, so registering there yields a registry that is
   complete before the run emits anything. No other code path may register
   values (no per-subsystem or fire-time registration — that was the
   architectural flaw of a previous, abandoned attempt).
2. **Per-run, never global.** A test-only in-process path executes multiple
   runs in one process; redaction state must be per-run (`SecretRedactor` is
   already built for this: cheap-clone shared state).
3. **Compose after the content pass.** Content-based redaction stays the
   universal baseline (it also catches credential-shaped values nobody
   declared, e.g. from `env.NAME`); the exact-match pass layers on top.
4. **Single entry point per surface.** Do NOT ship parallel "content-only" and
   "content+exact-match" variants of the same redaction API — a caller holding
   the run redactor could silently pick the weaker one. Every event-redaction
   call takes a `&SecretRedactor`; an empty redactor is the identity. A call
   site with genuinely no run scope passes `SecretRedactor::default()` **with
   a comment stating why no run secret can reach that surface**.
5. **Scope exact-match substitution to free-form-text fields.** Registered
   values can be low-entropy words; blind substitution across every event
   field would corrupt structural values (status enums, ids, event names) that
   legitimately contain the same word, breaking the typed event reparse.
   Restrict the exact-match walk to an explicit list of free-form-text
   property keys (see step 3). Keep the list minimal and comment it as an
   interim mechanism: a follow-up will derive it from field types. Do not
   build guard machinery around it.
6. **Ingest enforces; reads trust (team decision).** The architecture is:
   redact at the source (worker — this plan's registry + the existing content
   pass), enforce once more with a pattern-based pass where data enters shared
   storage (the server can only do pattern-based; it has no registry), and
   trust everywhere downstream. Do NOT add or extend any redaction on read
   paths (SSE, event detail, CLI rendering) in this PR — a separate change
   removes the existing read-side passes. If you find a read path missing
   data cleanliness, the fix belongs at source or ingest, never at output.

## Verified current state (as of main `8c3f035ea`, 2026-07-08 — re-verify before starting)

- `lib/crates/fabro-redact/src/secret_registry.rs`: `SecretRedactor` —
  `register(value)` (ignores empty/whitespace, dedups), `redact_into(&str)`
  (longest-first, replaces with the crate's `REDACTED` marker),
  `redact_json(Value)`, `is_empty()`; `Clone` + `Default`; shared interior
  state so clones observe registrations. **Currently has zero consumers.**
- `lib/crates/fabro-workflow/src/operations/start.rs:383`:
  `let secret_lookup = |name: &str| vault_token_lookup(vault_guard.as_deref(), name);`
  — consumed at `:390` (MCP servers), `:422` (docker config), `:446`
  (run-environment env), `:465` (prepare steps). Resolves; registers nothing.
- `lib/crates/fabro-workflow/src/event/redaction.rs`:
  `build_redacted_event_payload` / `redacted_event_json` apply
  `redact_json_value(normalize_json_value(...))` — content-based only.
- `lib/crates/fabro-workflow/src/pipeline/initialize.rs`: on prepare-step
  failure, constructs an error string embedding the resolved command and
  captured stderr, and emits `SetupCommandStarted` / `SetupCompleted` /
  `SetupFailed` events carrying resolved command text and exec-output tails.
- Event flow: emitter → run-event logger/sink (`event/sink.rs`,
  `runtime_store.rs` local run-store path) → stored payloads / SSE.

## Implementation

1. **Registry creation + registration** (`operations/start.rs`):
   - Create one `SecretRedactor` per run in `RunSession::new`; store it on
     `RunSession`.
   - Add `registered_vault_token_lookup(vault, &redactor, name)`: call
     `vault_token_lookup`, `register()` any returned value, return it. Swap
     the closure at `:383` to use it. All four consumers now feed the registry
     with no further changes.
2. **Thread the redactor to the event path.** Give the event sink / run-event
   logger the run's redactor (cheap clone) so every emitted event passes
   through the exact-match pass. Follow the existing wiring of the sink in
   `RunSession` (the logger is constructed there); make sure the local
   run-store backend receives redacted payloads too, and that anything
   reparsing to a typed event does so from the redacted payload so downstream
   sinks never see the raw value.
3. **Exact-match pass in `event/redaction.rs`**, composed after the content
   pass, skipped entirely when `redactor.is_empty()`:
   - Walk the event's `properties` object. For keys in the free-form-text
     list, apply `redactor.redact_json` to the whole subtree; for other keys,
     recurse (to reach nested listed keys such as `exec_output_tail.stderr`).
     Also apply `redact_into` to the top-level `node_label` string.
   - Free-form-text keys (grouped; keep as one `matches!`): command/script
     I/O: `command`, `script`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `output`, `input`,
     `arguments`, `exec_output_tail`, `tool_input`, `tool_output`; agent/LLM
     text: `prompt`, `response`, `answer`, `question`, `delta`, `text`,
     `message`, `reason`, `notes`, `preview`; errors: `error`,
     `error_message`, `failure`, `causes`, `details`, `description`;
     diffs/config: `diff`, `final_patch`, `workflow_config`,
     `workflow_source`; metadata text: `goal`, `subject`, `title`. Comment the
     list with: why it exists (low-entropy values vs structural fields) and
     that new free-form event fields must be added here until the
     type-derived replacement lands.
4. **Setup-failure error text** (`pipeline/initialize.rs`): pass the
   constructed failure message through `redactor.redact_into` before it
   becomes an `Error`. Thread the redactor into the initialize options along
   whatever path the session already passes options.
5. **Ingest-boundary pattern pass (server).** Locate where worker-shipped
   events and persisted run logs enter shared storage on the server (the
   HTTP event-append path the worker's run-store client posts to, plus any
   server-side log persistence). Verify whether a content-based pass runs
   there today; where it does not, apply `redact_json_value` /
   `redact_jsonl_line` at that ingest point, before the write. This is
   defense in depth for storage cleanliness — the server has no per-run
   registry, so pattern-based is the only pass it can perform. Content-based
   redaction is idempotent, so double application with the worker-side pass
   is harmless.
6. **Docs** (`docs/public/` run-configuration page): declared secrets are
   redacted regardless of shape on the run's structured surfaces (events,
   `progress.jsonl`, setup errors); command output is covered by content-based
   redaction plus exact-match where captured into those surfaces. State the
   boundary honestly — once a secret enters sandbox process env, text the
   sandbox re-emits is covered only where it is captured back into structured
   surfaces; do not claim a total guarantee.

## Tests (write failing-first; hermetic — temp-dir vaults, no ambient provider keys)

- A prepare step that fails while echoing a **low-entropy** declared secret
  (value `staging`) produces a `setup.failed` event and a run error in which
  the value is replaced by `REDACTED` — and a structural field legitimately
  containing the same word is untouched.
- After a run with declared secrets, no resolved secret value appears anywhere
  in the serialized stored events (scan the full `list_events` output).
- Content-based baseline unchanged: a high-entropy credential-shaped string in
  output is still redacted with an **empty** registry.
- Per-run isolation: two `RunSession`s in one process — each redacts its own
  registered value and not the other's.
- Empty registry fast path: event serialization is byte-identical to the
  current content-only output.
- Registration is boundary-time: a declared secret consumed only by MCP/prepare
  config is redacted from an event emitted before any stage runs.
- Ingest enforcement: an event posted to the server's append path containing a
  credential-shaped string is stored with that string redacted (pattern pass at
  ingest), independent of what the producer did.

## Acceptance / verification

- `cargo +nightly-2026-04-14 fmt --check --all`
- `cargo +nightly-2026-04-14 clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace`
- `cargo dev docs check` (docs page touched)
- No OpenAPI/wire change; TypeScript client untouched.

## Conventions

- Never print or log a resolved secret value, including from tests.
- Plain-English commit messages, PR text, and code comments — describe what
  the change does; no internal planning identifiers or plan-file names in
  anything that ships.
- PR description must state: the user-visible guarantee added (declared
  secrets redacted regardless of shape on structured surfaces), the known
  boundary (sandbox-crossing text covered where captured; live stream is a
  separate effort), and that exec-output tails are a follow-up surface.

FROM ubuntu:24.04

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        curl git ripgrep ca-certificates build-essential pkg-config libssl-dev unzip python3 \
        xvfb xfce4 xfce4-terminal x11vnc novnc dbus-x11 \
        libx11-6 libxrandr2 libxext6 libxrender1 libxfixes3 libxss1 libxtst6 libxi6 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install real Chromium (not the snap stub) via xtradeb PPA
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        software-properties-common curl gnupg \
    && add-apt-repository -y ppa:xtradeb/apps \
    && apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends chromium \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Wrapper: Chromium needs --no-sandbox when running as root in a container,
# and --disable-dev-shm-usage avoids crashes from small /dev/shm
RUN printf '#!/bin/bash\nexec /usr/bin/chromium --no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage "$@"\n' \
        > /usr/local/bin/chromium-wrapper \
    && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/chromium-wrapper

# Make the wrapper the default in the system .desktop file and via alternatives
RUN sed -i 's|^Exec=.*|Exec=/usr/local/bin/chromium-wrapper %U|' \
        /usr/share/applications/chromium.desktop \
    && update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/x-www-browser x-www-browser \
        /usr/local/bin/chromium-wrapper 100

# Tell XFCE's exo-open that Chromium is the WebBrowser helper (system-wide)
RUN mkdir -p /etc/xdg/xfce4 /usr/share/xfce4/helpers \
    && printf 'WebBrowser=custom-WebBrowser\n' > /etc/xdg/xfce4/helpers.rc \
    && printf '[Desktop Entry]\n\
Version=1.0\n\
Type=X-XFCE-Helper\n\
Name=Chromium\n\
Icon=chromium\n\
X-XFCE-Category=WebBrowser\n\
X-XFCE-CommandsWithParameter=/usr/local/bin/chromium-wrapper "%%s"\n\
X-XFCE-Commands=/usr/local/bin/chromium-wrapper\n' \
        > /usr/share/xfce4/helpers/custom-WebBrowser.desktop

# GitHub CLI
RUN curl -fsSL https://cli.github.com/packages/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg \
        | dd of=/usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg \
    && echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg] https://cli.github.com/packages stable main" \
        | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/github-cli.list > /dev/null \
    && apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends gh \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Rust
RUN curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y
ENV PATH="/root/.cargo/bin:${PATH}"
RUN rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-04-14 --profile minimal --component clippy,rustfmt
RUN cargo install cargo-nextest --locked
ENV CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0

# Bun
RUN curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
ENV PATH="/root/.bun/bin:${PATH}"

WORKDIR /root

script.String: command -v cargo >/dev/null || { curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y && sudo ln -sf $HOME/.cargo/bin/* /usr/local/bin/; }; cargo --version 2>&1

# Simplify: Code Review and Cleanup

Review all changes for reuse, quality, and efficiency. Fix any issues found. Feel free to use any sub agents you need.

## Phase 1: Identify Changes

Run git diff (or git diff HEAD if there are staged changes) to see what changed. If there are no git changes, review the most recently modified files that the user mentioned or that you edited earlier in this conversation. (You may already have the changes in context, if so, feel free to skip this part)

## Phase 2: Launch Three Review Agents in Parallel

Use the Agent tool to launch all three agents concurrently in a single message. Pass each agent the full diff so it has the complete context.

### Agent 1: Code Reuse Review

For each change:

1. Search for existing utilities and helpers that could replace newly written code. Use Grep to find similar patterns elsewhere in the codebase — common locations are utility directories, shared modules, and files adjacent to the changed ones.
2. Flag any new function that duplicates existing functionality. Suggest the existing function to use instead.
3. Flag any inline logic that could use an existing utility — hand-rolled string manipulation, manual path handling, custom environment checks, ad-hoc type guards, and similar patterns are common candidates.

Note: This is a greenfield app, so focus on maximizing simplicity and don't worry about changing things to achieve it.

### Agent 2: Code Quality Review

Review the same changes for hacky patterns:

1. Redundant state: state that duplicates existing state, cached values that could be derived, observers/effects that could be direct calls
2. Parameter sprawl: adding new parameters to a function instead of generalizing or restructuring existing ones
3. Copy-paste with slight variation: near-duplicate code blocks that should be unified with a shared abstraction
4. Leaky abstractions: exposing internal details that should be encapsulated, or breaking existing abstraction boundaries
5. Stringly-typed code: using raw strings where constants, enums (string unions), or branded types already exist in the codebase

Note: This is a greenfield app, so be aggressive in optimizing quality.

### Agent 3: Efficiency Review

Review the same changes for efficiency:

1. Unnecessary work: redundant computations, repeated file reads, duplicate network/API calls, N+1 patterns
2. Missed concurrency: independent operations run sequentially when they could run in parallel
3. Hot-path bloat: new blocking work added to startup or per-request/per-render hot paths
4. Unnecessary existence checks: pre-checking file/resource existence before operating (TOCTOU anti-pattern) — operate directly and handle the error
5. Memory: unbounded data structures, missing cleanup, event listener leaks
6. Overly broad operations: reading entire files when only a portion is needed, loading all items when filtering for one

## Phase 3: Fix Issues

Wait for all three agents to complete. Aggregate their findings and fix each issue directly. If a finding is a false positive or not worth addressing, note it and move on — do not argue with the finding, just skip it.

When done, briefly summarize what was fixed (or confirm the code was already clean).
The preflight lint step failed. Read the build output from context and fix all clippy lint warnings.

Fabro workflows can declare vault secrets in run config via `secrets.NAME`
tokens (MCP transport env, run-environment env, prepare-step commands/env,
docker config). Those tokens resolve server-side at the run boundary in
`RunSession::new`. Redaction of run output (events, `progress.jsonl`, error
text) is currently **content-based only**: pattern + entropy matching in

secret whose value looks ordinary — e.g. a secret whose value is `staging`,
`db-prod-3`, or `hunter2` trips neither entropy nor any pattern rule, and
today leaks **verbatim** into emitted events and error messages. That is a
live gap: the user explicitly declared the value secret, and the system does
not honor it.

**Goal:** register every resolved declared-secret value into a per-run
exact-match registry at the single place secrets resolve, and apply that
registry (composed after the content-based pass) to the run's structured
output surfaces: emitted events and setup-failure error text.

Design rules (fixed — the "why" for each is inline):

1. **One registration point.** Every secret value flows through the one
   boundary lookup closure, so registering there yields a registry that is
   complete before the run emits anything. No other code path may register
   values (no per-subsystem or fire-time registration — that was the
   architectural flaw of a previous, abandoned attempt).
2. **Per-run, never global.** A test-only in-process path executes multiple
   runs in one process; redaction state must be per-run (`SecretRedactor` is
   already built for this: cheap-clone shared state).
3. **Compose after the content pass.** Content-based redaction stays the
   universal baseline (it also catches credential-shaped values nobody
   declared, e.g. from `env.NAME`); the exact-match pass layers on top.
4. **Single entry point per surface.** Do NOT ship parallel "content-only" and

   the run redactor could silently pick the weaker one. Every event-redaction
   call takes a `&SecretRedactor`; an empty redactor is the identity. A call

   a comment stating why no run secret can reach that surface**.
5. **Scope exact-match substitution to free-form-text fields.** Registered
   values can be low-entropy words; blind substitution across every event
   field would corrupt structural values (status enums, ids, event names) that
   legitimately contain the same word, breaking the typed event reparse.

## Tests (write failing-first; hermetic — temp-dir vaults, no ambient provider keys)

- A prepare step that fails while echoing a **low-entropy** declared secret
  (value `staging`) produces a `setup.failed` event and a run error in which
  the value is replaced by `REDACTED` — and a structural field legitimately
  containing the same word is untouched.
- After a run with declared secrets, no resolved secret value appears anywhere
  in the serialized stored events (scan the full `list_events` output).
- Content-based baseline unchanged: a high-entropy credential-shaped string in
  output is still redacted with an **empty** registry.
- Per-run isolation: two `RunSession`s in one process — each redacts its own
  registered value and not the other's.
- Empty registry fast path: event serialization is byte-identical to the
  current content-only output.
- Registration is boundary-time: a declared secret consumed only by MCP/prepare
  config is redacted from an event emitted before any stage runs.
- Ingest enforcement: an event posted to the server's append path containing a
  credential-shaped string is stored with that string redacted (pattern pass at
  ingest), independent of what the producer did.

- `cargo +nightly-2026-04-14 clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace`

## Conventions

- Never print or log a resolved secret value, including from tests.
- Plain-English commit messages, PR text, and code comments — describe what
  the change does; no internal planning identifiers or plan-file names in
  anything that ships.
- PR description must state: the user-visible guarantee added (declared
  secrets redacted regardless of shape on structured surfaces), the known
  boundary (sandbox-crossing text covered where captured; live stream is a
  separate effort), and that exec-output tails are a follow-up surface.
